thread.title_full: Bloomington man claimed he was firing his gun at logs in his backyard - NewsBreak

author: Mike Hanks
title: Bloomington man claimed he was firing his gun at logs in his backyard - NewsBreak
text:
By Mike Hanks ,
18 hours ago A 40-year-old Bloomington man was charged with one count of reckless discharge of a weapon accused of firing a gun in the backyard of his home.
Police officers were dispatched to the 8300 block of 12th Avenue at approximately 4:30 p.m. June 2 following reports that either fireworks were being set off or gunshots were being fired. Residents initially reporting the sound were uncertain what street the sound was originating from, and subsequent callers reported hearing what sounded like the racking of a firearm, and a male muttering something, according to a criminal complaint filed in Hennepin County District Court.
The additional information pointed officers toward the 8300 block of 12th Avenue, and officers arriving in the vicinity were informed a resident reported hearing the suspect telling his dog to get out of the way, and that he was slurring his words. Officers then heard two gunshots from the backyard of the suspect’s home, the complaint explained.
The police department used a drone to help survey the suspect’s yard, set up a perimeter around his residence and issued a shelter-in-place notice to the neighborhood while assessing the situation, according to Bloomington Police Cmdr. Eric Kittelson.
An officer was able to survey the suspect’s backyard from the roof of a neighboring garage, and gave the suspect verbal commands, which he followed, Kittelson noted.
The suspect appeared to be intoxicated, and a shotgun was lying in the grass approximately 15 feet from the suspect when officers entered his backyard. He was arrested and had four shotgun shells in one of his pockets, the complaint noted.
Following his arrest, the suspect told the police that he was mad about his job and was from the country, where it was common to shoot at logs. He said he did not think about the fact he was within the city limits, and that he was not shooting at anyone, just logs on the ground. He said he may have consumed one beer, but did not remember drinking, according to the complaint.
He submitted to a preliminary breath test following his arrest and registered a blood-alcohol concentration of 0.24%, the complaint noted.
A witness that lives near the suspect’s home told the police that he heard three loud blasts in a 15- to 20-minute period and could hear the suspect speaking to his dog and slurring his words. Following one gunshot, branches fell from a tree in the vicinity, the complaint explained.
A search of the suspect’s home turned up additional guns, but nobody was in the house at the time of the arrest, Kittelson said.
If convicted of reckless discharge of a firearm, the suspect faces up to two years in prison and a $5,000 fine.
Carjacking
A 40-year-old Hibbing woman was charged with one count of carjacking, accused of taking a Bloomington woman’s vehicle following a confrontation.
Police officers were dispatched to the 1900 block of 86th Street East at approximately 11:35 a.m. June 3 following a report that the suspect had pushed a woman and taken her car. Officers spoke with a 38-year-old woman who said she had been sitting in her vehicle outside of an apartment building and was waiting for her son. The suspect approached the car, opened the door and told the woman to give her the vehicle’s keys, according to a criminal complaint filed in Hennepin County District Court.
The woman refused and stepped out of her vehicle. The suspect continued to demand the woman’s keys and was holding something black in her hand, which the woman thought could be a weapon. The suspect allegedly asked the woman if she wanted to live or die, at which point the woman said she handed over her keys. The suspect then entered the woman’s car and drove off, the complaint explained.
A witness reported seeing the woman wrestling with the suspect before the suspect drove off in the car, the complaint noted.
Security video from the apartment building showed the suspect walking north through the building’s parking lot, passing the woman’s vehicle and turning around to confront the woman. The video also showed the woman and the suspect appearing to grapple over an item in the woman’s hand before the suspect drove away in the car, according to the complaint.
The woman’s vehicle was spotted hours later in Savage and was eventually stopped in Burnsville. The suspect was driving the vehicle and matched an image of the carjacking perpetrator from the surveillance video. She was initially taken to a hospital for a medical issue and discharged after a few hours of monitoring, at which point she was taken into custody and transported to Bloomington for booking, the complaint explained.
The suspect did not go quietly, however, as she struck an officer in the head while being taken into custody, the complaint noted.
Following her arrest, the suspect told the police that she heard sirens while in Bloomington, thought she was in a bad part of town and approached the 38-year-old woman, demanding the keys to her car. The suspect claimed that she was scared and needed to go to a hospital at the time of the incident, according to the complaint.
If convicted, the suspect faces up to 10 years in prison and a $20,000 fine.
The suspect was charged as a Hibbing resident but had a Savage address when she was charged in November 2025 with deprivation of custodial rights involving her children and their father, who has sole custody of the children.
The suspect’s criminal history also includes a conviction for manufacturing counterfeit currency. Along with a co-conspirator, she was arrested at a Bloomington hotel in June 2008, where they were found to be in possession of materials commonly used to manufacture counterfeit currency, according to the U.S. Attorney’s Office.
Angry roommate
A 19-year-old Bloomington man was charged with one gross misdemeanor count of domestic assault following a fight with a roommate at a Bloomington group home.
Police officers were dispatched to the 5400 block of Old Shakopee Circle West at approximately 8:20 p.m. June 2 following a report of a fight between two residents of the home. The suspect had blood on his clothes and shoes, and said it was his 33-year-old roommate’s blood, Kittelson said.
The 33-year-old man had blood on his clothing, as well, and was still bleeding from his mouth. The man appeared to have bruises on his head and initially declined to give a statement regarding his injuries, according to a criminal complaint filed in Hennepin County District Court.
There was also blood on the man’s bed and bedroom floor, a bedroom he shares with the suspect, the complaint noted.
When questioned by a police officer, the suspect said he won the fight, which started because the 33-year-old man wanted the suspect to apologize to another resident of the home for allegedly calling that resident a derogatory name. The suspect said he threw the first punch, claiming the 33-year-old man threw punches in retaliation, the complaint explained.
Staff members of the group home said they heard the suspect yelling, and minutes later he was following the 33-year-old man downstairs while screaming at him. The staff attempted to intervene and told the 33-year-old man he could move to another bedroom, but he declined, the complaint said.
When the suspect was later heard screaming in their bedroom, a staff member entered the room and found the suspect with his arm wrapped around the 33-year-old man’s neck from behind, according to the complaint.
The suspect was convicted of assault in May, the complaint noted. In that case from October 2025, the suspect was accused of shoplifting at a Brooklyn Center grocery store. After initially fighting with a store employee who attempted to detain the suspect, the suspect returned to the store with a stop sign and post from the parking lot in an effort to continue the fight, according to a criminal complaint.
summary: 18 hours ago A 40-year-old Bloomington man was charged with one count of reckless discharge of a weapon accused of firing a gun in the backyard of his home. The suspect approached the car, opened the door and told the woman to give her the vehicle’s keys, according to a criminal complaint filed in Hennepin County District Court. She was initially taken to a hospital for a medical issue and discharged after a few hours of monitoring, at which point she was taken into custody and transported to Bloomington for booking, the complaint explained.
